tools.name: check_package
tools.description: Public safety verdict for ONE package (optionally one version) from CyberXYZ's global threat data: known-malicious releases (always shown in full), advisories, commit-level analysis and version anomalies. Call it BEFORE adding or installing an npm, PyPI, Go or NuGet dependency. `decision`: block or

tools.name: get_vulnerability
tools.description: Full detail for one advisory id (CVE-..., GHSA-..., or an OSV id such as PYSEC-...): every affected package (`affected_packages`: package, ecosystem, ranges, fixed), the primary one's version ranges and fixed version, severity, CVSS, EPSS (probability of exploitation in 30 days), CISA KEV (exploited

tools.name: search
tools.description: Find a package by name across every ecosystem (exact match first, then prefix, then most advisories), with its advisory count and worst severity. Use it when you do not know a package's ecosystem or exact spelling; then call package_info or check_package.

tools.name: model_risk
tools.description: CyberXYZ's public report on a Hugging Face model's install risk: risk level, XYZ score, the driving reason, the worst dependencies and recent risk events. verdict UNKNOWN (not watched, pending, gated) is not safe: ask the user. Signing in adds every reason, all flagged dependencies and per-file load

tools.name: package_info
tools.description: CyberXYZ's public report for a package: every published advisory (CVE/GHSA ids, severity, CVSS, EPSS, KEV, affected ranges, fixed version), malicious-package records in full, how many packages depend on it, what it pulls in (counts and worst severity) and AI-model usage. Package-level; for a verdict

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.
